Why go: a slow, social day on a traditional Thai junk

Red Dragon is a 78 ft teak junk with red sails, wide sun decks, shaded dining space and a jacuzzi. At about 11 knots it is slow compared with a speedboat, but that is the point: the day is spent eating, swimming and lying in the sun rather than holding on. It is also big. With room for up to 74 guests, it is one of the few boats on Koh Samui that can take a wedding party or a company group in one go.

The southern islands charter passes the Five Islands, stops at Koh Tan for snorkelling and kayaking, serves a Thai buffet on board and visits Koh Madsum (Pig Island) before a sunset cruise home. The Ang Thong day adds snorkelling at Koh Wao, a beach stop and the Emerald Lake walk.

Who it suits, and who should choose something else

  • Good for: large groups, multi-generation families and celebrations.
  • Choose something else if you are a small group in a hurry: a private speedboat covers more ground for less.
  • Just two of you? The sunset cruise guide lists shared options.

Good to know

  • Ang Thong: closed every year from 1 November to 15 December.
  • Stability: a big wooden junk rolls less than a speedboat, so it suits guests who get seasick.
  • Jacuzzi: keep children supervised around it and at the boarding ladder.
  • Weather: the captain chooses sheltered routes in the monsoon. If the trip is cancelled for weather, you choose a new date or a full refund.

Planning a group charter

For groups over about 20, decide early on drinks: bringing your own with the corkage fee is usually cheaper than a running bar tab. Tell us about dietary needs so the buffet can be adjusted, and about elderly guests so the crew can plan easy boarding at the jetty.
